title: Scanning what the code exposes: Checkov, Trivy, tfsec and Terrascan

videos.script: A colleague of Ana's opens a pull request. One new file, eight lines, SSH for maintenance. The reviewer is busy, the description sounds fine, and it gets approved. {{pr}} Inside it, port 22 is open to every address on the internet. A scanner is a reviewer that does not get tired. It reads the Terraform files, holds each resource against a catalogue of rules, and names the file and the line. {{finding}} This lesson runs three of them on the same code: Checkov, Trivy and tfsec. They agree on most of it. Where they disagree, you learn what a scanner really is. One of them never saw the SSH rule at all, and said nothing. {{three}} You will silence a finding the right way, with a reason and an expiry date. And you will catch a value the files never contained, by scanning the plan instead. {{plan}} Then comes the part no tool does for you. A small network produced thirteen findings. Deciding which of them should stop a merge, and which are noise, is a judgement about your system. The scanner only knows the text. {{triage}}
